```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

Several things you might expect are missing on purpose. Each one below says why,
and what would change our mind. If you need one of them today, the
[cyCONDOR article](with-cycondor.html) shows how to run both tools on the same
dataset.

## Harmony and CytoNorm

Batch correction itself is here. `--correct-batch` does monotone quantile
alignment and refuses when batch and group are confounded.

What is missing is those two implementations specifically. Both are heavy
dependencies, and neither declines to run when correcting the batch and deleting
your finding are the same operation. That refusal is the behaviour cyRAVEN
treats as the point of the feature.

## Phenograph

FlowSOM covers the same need and is faster at these cell counts. Phenograph picks
its own cluster count instead of taking it as a setting, which is genuinely
useful, but it needs `Rphenograph` or `Rphenoannoy`, and neither is on CRAN or
Bioconductor. Depending on a GitHub-only package would break the reproducibility
guarantee the container is there to provide.

Worth adding when the number of clusters becomes a question you are asking rather
than a parameter you are setting.

## diffcyt, limma and mixed models

The rank tests cyRAVEN runs answer the same questions without the distributional
assumptions, which is the better trade at single-digit n per group.

Worth adding when your groups reach fifteen or more samples each. That is roughly
where the empirical Bayes prior starts earning its place and where a mixed model
can absorb repeated measures properly.

## Per-marker cofactors

`derive_cofactor()` already works out per-marker candidates and returns them in
`attr(cf, "per_marker")`. Applying them is not wired up.

Doing so would change the arcsinh scale channel by channel, which moves every
threshold, every marker median and every distance in the UMAP. That is a large
methodological change and it cannot be validated without rerunning and rereading
every gating QC figure. The data needed to make the decision is collected, so if
your gating QC shows channels whose backgrounds genuinely differ in scale, the
argument for switching can be made from your own run.

## Pseudotime and trajectories

A trajectory assumes a continuous developmental process. Peripheral blood
immunophenotyping panels mostly measure populations that have finished
differentiating, and a trajectory fitted to those is an artefact of the fitting
rather than a finding.

Worth adding when the panel gains a genuine developmental axis. cyCONDOR wraps
diffusion maps and Slingshot if you need one now.

## Supervised cell-type classifiers

Label transfer models are standard elsewhere. Here the labels come from a gating
specification you wrote, so a classifier trained on them can only learn to
reproduce that specification, errors included.

The unsupervised clustering cross-check is the better tool for the same job,
because it does not consult your labels at all.

Worth adding when an externally annotated reference dataset exists to train
against.

## Reading FlowJo workspaces

cyRAVEN writes FlowJo files, it does not read them. Parsing a `.wsp` workspace
needs `CytoML` and `flowWorkspace`, a heavy pair of dependencies, for the inverse
of what the package is for.

Worth adding when manual FlowJo gates need to be the input rather than the
output.

## Cell-level differential expression

Absent on purpose, for the reason the whole package is built around: an FCS file
holds as many cells as somebody chose to acquire, so a test over pooled cells has
a sample size set by acquisition time. The tools that do offer a cell-level
Wilcoxon ship it with a warning against using it.

The cell-level view is available descriptively in `subcluster_marker_shifts.csv`,
which carries effect sizes and no p-values. That is the honest form for this kind
of number.

## Building a compensation matrix

cyRAVEN applies a spillover matrix when a file carries one. It will not build one
from single-stain controls. That belongs in acquisition software where you can
see what you are adjusting.
